projects.description: An agentic skills framework & software development methodology that works.

release.body:
This release retunes brainstorming after its rebuild in v7.0.0. Many of you told us, rightly, that the new default questions got annoying fast and felt formulaic. Brainstorming now digs for context before it asks anything, and tries to ask better questions. We expect to keep tuning it, but we think it's better than it was.

It also trims three long skills so they better survive compaction on Claude Code, and changes the issue and PR templates to ask for a summary written by a human.

### Brainstorming

- **It digs for context first.** In an existing project, or when you point it at a spec, plan, or files, it reads them before its first message and doesn't ask what they already answer. (#2560)
- **It tries to ask better questions.** v7.0.0 opened every session the same way: an offer to skip the questions, then a generic question about "the moment you wished this existed." Now, when you've already said what you want, it plays your request back with what it found in the project and asks about the one thing still open. Later questions build on your answers and on what it found, and say what the answer would change. (#2560, #2571)
- **It offers to skip the questions only when it started on its own.** If you asked for brainstorming by name or with `/brainstorming`, it no longer offers to skip it. (#2560)
- **It lays out the approaches and writes a design doc before building.** It presents two or three ways to build the thing, recommends one, and asks you to pick. Then it writes a design doc, a short one for a small change, and builds nothing until you approve it. Some of you saw it skip the doc and start building; in one of our test scenarios, it skipped the doc without asking in 24 of 24 runs before this change and 3 of 24 after. (#2571)

Thanks to @mbcrawfo for opening #25

projects.description: Persistent Context Across Sessions for Every Agent –  Captures everything your agent does during sessions, compresses it with AI, and injects relevant context back into future sessions. Works with Claude Code, OpenClaw, Codex, Gemini, Hermes, Copilot, OpenCode + More

release.body:
## My Work: refresh stays on your agent, and a Feedback button (#5190)

When My Work's automatic refresh got an answer from Claude Code that claude-mem refused (most often a review over 1,200 characters), the whole refresh moved on to the next logged-in agent. On machines with Codex installed, that meant hidden codex exec --ephemeral runs on the owner's ChatGPT account, even with CLAUDE_MEM_PROVIDER=claude (#5189: about 230 runs in four days).

- A refused answer now ends that refresh on the agent that gave it. The next scheduled run tries the same agent again, with the existing failure backoff. An agent that can't run at all (not signed in, crashed) still hands the run to the next one.
- Feedback button in the My Work header, next to Star. It opens a short "My Work feedback" issue form.

## Note-taker always uses the newest Haiku (#5195)

The note-taker's default model is now Claude Code's haiku alias, which always resolves to the newest Haiku, instead of a pinned Haiku 4.5 ID. Saved settings that still carry the shipped pinned ID move to the alias on upgrade. A model you typed yourself is left alone. The repo's CLAUDE.md now states this as policy: never pin a dated model ID as a default.

## My Work and the worker

- Activity-driven background rebuilds of My Work are coalesced, so an open My Work page no longer rebuilds on every database commit (#5133, mitigates #5124).
- Work View waits for the database to finish starting before it builds (#5157).
- The viewer's processing status reconciles after a stream gap (#5139).
- Daily worker logs older than CLAUDE_MEM_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS (default 30, 0 keeps forever) are pruned. Today's and yesterday's files are always kept (#5186).

- Named environments inside a parent Git repository can declare explicit inherita

# DeepTutor v1.7.0 Release Notes

**Release Date:** 2026.10.28

Building on [v1.6.15](past_releases/ver1-6-15.md), v1.7.0 brings modular installation, a refreshed learning workspace, block-based notebooks with Dito, and narrated video lessons. Full-app upgrades now use `deeptutor[full]`; existing runtime data remains separate from the installed packages.

## What's New

### Install the parts you use

`deeptutor` now provides core chat, CLI, and SDK; `deeptutor[full]` selects the Web app and standard feature modules. The `deeptutor-cli` package becomes a compatibility alias. Inspect installed, enabled, and ready states with `deeptutor module list`, then enable, disable, install, or remove modules while the app is stopped. Dependency checks protect required modules, and removal preserves user data.

### A workspace organized around learning

Modern and Classic layouts offer different navigation arrangements. Home brings together Chat, the Task Board, Learning notebook, and Calendar; Learning and Resources keep study activities and materials accessible. Customize Chat modes, controls, and starting prompts, or choose which learning methods appear on the New learning page. Conversation and resource navigation retain their workspace boundaries.

### Notebook pages with Dito beside them

The Learning notebook replaces the former Co-Writer editor with pages, subpages, and blocks. Import Word documents, insert source records from Favorites, discuss a passage with Dito, and review proposed edits before accepting them. Export pages as Markdown or Word. Favorites hold saved source records; notebook pages hold your own writing and understanding.

### Video lessons and free read-aloud

Choose Video Lesson to generate a lesson that plays directly in the browser, with captions and opti

projects.description: Search your computer by what's in your files: photos, PDFs, documents, recordings, videos and code. On-device on Mac, Windows and Linux, built on Google DeepMind's EmbeddingGemma 2.

release.body:
Fixes for the ten days since 0.6.1, with a lot of them from people who sent pull requests, and spreadsheets and presentations as a new kind of file.

Fixed:

- Battery drain after the first pass. Two causes: a folder where something rewrites files all the time (a database, logs, a build) made DigUp re-scan every folder every few seconds, and iCloud Drive or Google Drive folders made every scan take minutes. Changes that couldn't matter are ignored now, and the crawl no longer asks the cloud about each file. (#68, #101 by @astelmach20; #106, #107 by @afalk42)
- A folder you chose is read whole, whatever it holds. A home folder with its dotfiles in git, or a repo of notes and pictures, used to count as a code project and keep only its screenshots. (#105)
- Settings → Folders says why files aren't searchable: "N not read" next to each folder opens the reasons (inside code projects, only in the cloud, types DigUp doesn't read, a Photos library). (#105, #43)
- The progress bar no longer starts over when new files arrive mid-pass. (#52, from #53 by @dr0pd34d)
- Resume right after Pause starts indexing again; it used to stay stopped until the next change. (#50, from #51 by @dr0pd34d)
- The search panel opens over a fullscreen app while a DigUp window is open or minimized, instead of switching Spaces. (#73, #131 by @TLXyloph)
- A PDF with broken metadata no longer crashes indexing. (#41, #42 by @dr0pd34d)
- Copy-protected songs (.m4p) are skipped instead of failing one by one. (#108, #109 by @afalk42)
- The "Open code in" picker follows what you choose. (#83, #74 by @maniksundar)
- Keyword search is faster on big indexes: the database is memory-mapped, 18–20% on a 29,000-vector index here. (#93, #94 by @Hevarh1, with @Bondyboy2001's measurements)
- Tiny stub files (`DEBUG=true`

release.body:
Anatomy can now share what it makes. Ask your agent to publish a finished figure and it lands in the [community gallery](https://github.com/wheresryan22/anatomy-community), with its prompt, model, and how long it took.

### Install or update

```bash
npx skills add wheresryan22/anatomy
```

Or download `anatomy.zip` below and unzip it into `~/.claude/skills`. The latest zip is always at https://github.com/wheresryan22/anatomy/releases/latest/download/anatomy.zip

### New

- **Publish to the community gallery.** Make a figure as usual, then say *"publish this figure to the Anatomy community gallery"*. Your agent asks for a title, an id and your GitHub name, shows exactly what it will send, and opens the pull request after you say yes; it makes a fork for you if you need one. Only the figure's source is sent: the gallery rebuilds it in a locked sandbox, checks it, and photographs it. (`scripts/publish.mjs`, `references/publish.md`)
- **Time and tokens, recorded for you.** In Claude Code, publishing reads how long the figure took and how many tokens it used from the session's own log, from your request to the request to publish, leaving out idle gaps and cache reads. The plan shows both before anything is sent; `--minutes` and `--tokens` set them by hand in other agents.
- **More agents.** Anatomy runs in OpenCode and Codex as well as Claude Code, and the gallery knows Antigravity too.

### Fixed

38 fixes, mostly in the checks that keep figures honest:

- **Browser checks** start on Linux, fail when a page doesn't load or a step throws, time out cleanly, reject unknown or misspelled actions, and clean up after Chrome exits early.
- **The geometry audit** measures transformed, arced, clipped and tapered shapes by their true bounds, converges on large figures, and keeps sli
